text:
Dmitri Simashev waited until his first NHL goal to make it count. The Mammoth defenseman scored twice, including the overtime winner 1:44 into the extra period, as Utah erased a two-goal deficit and beat Tampa Bay 5-4. The Coyotes drafted him sixth overall in 2023 out of Lokomotiv Yaroslavl's system, and he had one goal in 56 KHL games last season before tonight.

For two periods, Tampa Bay looked like the team in control. The Lightning built a 4-1 lead in the second period, helped by Pontus Holmberg's goal on what our numbers rated a 3% chance, and Tampa Bay led the first period in expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the count) 1.68 to 0.70. Then the game turned. Anders Lee and Simashev scored 2:23 apart late in the second to tie it at 4, and Utah owned the third, out-chancing TBL 1.66 to 0.67 in expected goals. Kailer Yamamoto had the best look that didn't go in, a 26% chance in the third that Dennis Hildeby stopped. Hildeby allowed one goal more than the 28 shots against him deserved, while Karel Vejmelka was close to even on his night.

Across the full game, our numbers say Utah deserved to win 57% of the time, meaning that share of simulated replays of every shot ended in a Mammoth win. Our facts don't carry streaks or standings for either club, so we'll leave the stakes at this: Utah showed it can absorb an early punch and wait for the game to tilt its way, while Tampa Bay has to ask how a three-goal lead turned into an overtime loss.
